## Logging

The service derives the whole render's verbosity from its own effective .NET log level and surfaces the R/Quarto child diagnostics back into `ILogger` (see `ReportLogging` + `ExternalProcessReportProducer` / `QuartoReportProducer`).

- **One dial, from the .NET level.** `ReportLogging.EffectiveMinLevel(Logger)` is mapped to the child controls in each producer's `GetProcessStartInfo`: `NEOIPC_LOG_LEVEL` (`Trace→debug`, `Debug→verbose`, `Information→normal`, `Warning+→quiet`) drives the R `logger` namespaces — including neoipcr's DHIS2 query trace, which only appears at `verbose`/`debug` — and `NEOIPC_LOG_FILE` is the structured file the R side writes. Quarto's `--log-level` is derived too but **floored at `info`** (`Trace/Debug→debug`, else `info`).
- **Why Quarto is floored at `info`.** Quarto captures Pandoc's stderr and re-emits every line — whatever its real severity — as one of its own `INFO` records, so `--log-level warning` would drop Pandoc warnings *and errors* before they reach the log file. Keeping Quarto at `info` guarantees the lines are captured; the drain then recovers each Pandoc line's true severity from its `[ERROR]`/`[WARNING]`/`[INFO]` prefix. The lualatex PDF engine and the knitr R engine are flattened the same way — Quarto re-emits their output as its own records, and (unlike Pandoc) without a per-line severity prefix — so the drain recovers each **only on a failed render** (`exitCode != 0`, leaving benign warnings on a successful render alone). **LaTeX** is recovered *structurally*: Quarto's `writeError` emits `error("compilation failed- …")` then the extracted detail then a `see …log` pointer, so the drain anchors on that block and re-attributes the whole thing to `.LaTeX` — content-agnostic, so **any** `findLatexError` shape is caught (the `l.<n>` context, the fixed `No pages of output`, or a future guidance string like 1.10's luaotfload-fallback message; keying on the stable writeError *structure* rather than the shifting detail *content* is what makes it future-proof). **R** is recovered from knitr's **red-ANSI** colourising plus an R error signal; the recovery is **level-agnostic** (so it still fires if [quarto-dev#12799](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/12799) later promotes knitr errors to ERROR at source), and its **colour-independent** signals — knitr's untranslated `Quitting from` frame plus the native-crash markers (`caught segfault` / `R is aborting now`) — match without colour, so recovery survives `NO_COLOR` **and** a non-English `LC_ALL`. Localized signals ride the red gate instead: the rlang `! ` bullet (punctuation, so itself locale-proof) and base R's `Error:`. (`Execution halted` is matched colour-free too but, being R-translated, only helps under an English `LC_ALL`.) The red gate itself is reliable only because `GetProcessStartInfo` **scrubs `NO_COLOR`** from the child env (Deno gates its colour on `!Deno.noColor`). Benign engine output — the LuaHBTeX banner, R progress — carries no signal and stays on `.Quarto`; the emitted text has its SGR colour codes stripped.
- **Drain on success and failure.** After the child exits, `DrainDiagnostics` re-emits the two structured files — the R `layout_json` file and (for Quarto) `quarto-log.json` — into `ILogger`. This runs on the **success** path too, so a successful render's DHIS2 query trace is no longer discarded. It is inherently post-process (the files are complete only once the child exits) and emits **two ordered per-source blocks**: Quarto records carry no per-record timestamp, so the Quarto and R blocks are not interleaved with each other; each is chronological in its own file order.
- **Per-source categories.** Each render logs under a tree rooted at `NeoIPC.Reporting.Render.<report>` (`<report>` = `Partner-Report`/`Reference-Report`/`Validation-Report`): `.Quarto`, `.Pandoc`, `.LaTeX` (the `writeError` block for a failed PDF compile, recovered to `Error` — see above), `.R.report`, `.R.common` (the toolkit's shared `common/` layer), `.R.neoipcr` (keyed by the R record's `ns` field). R output reaches the log two ways: its **structured** `layout_json` records (drained by `DrainRLogAsync`, attributed by namespace to `.R.neoipcr`/`.R.common`/`.R.report`), and the **raw knitr stderr** Quarto captures onto its own stream — recovered to `.R.report` at `Error` when a failed render's record carries an R error signal (level-agnostic; the origin namespace is not recoverable from the Quarto stream, so it lands on the generic `.R.report`). Each entry emits through its own sub-logger, so operators tune any one source via `Logging:LogLevel:NeoIPC.Reporting.Render.*` — **both directions**: a successful render emits Quarto/Pandoc INFO progress at the default `Information` level, so quieten a source (e.g. `…<report>.Quarto` → `Warning` to drop render-progress chatter) or raise one (e.g. `…<report>.R.neoipcr` → `Debug` for the DHIS2 query trace). The child-process verbosity is derived from the **minimum** effective level across this sub-tree, so raising a single source actually makes the child *write* that source's finer records, not just pass them at emit time.  `appsettings.Development.json` sets the whole `NeoIPC.Reporting.Render` tree to `Debug`.
- **Correlation.** Each render opens a `RenderId` log scope (its workdir name), with a nested `ProcessId` scope once the child starts, so concurrent renders' drained entries stay attributable. `appsettings.json` enables console `IncludeScopes` so these appear in the emitted output.
- **GDPR.** The DHIS2 query trace is **URL + HTTP status + row count only — never response bodies** (the boundary lives in neoipcr's `log_dhis2_request`). Do not add any drain path that could emit a response body. Note that the LaTeX/R error-recovery above can promote engine output — which may quote report content (a TeX `l.<n>` line echoes the typeset source; an R error can name a value) — to `Error` on a dedicated channel. This does not widen the data-protection boundary: it is the same promotion the pre-existing Pandoc recovery already does, it only changes the level/channel of records Quarto already emitted verbatim on `.Quarto` at the default level, the audience is unchanged (the operator, who already holds the rendered report), and the `log_dhis2_request` boundary is untouched.
